title: Configuring Google Chrome to Use a PAC File

blocks.text: To redirect your web traffic to the Zscaler cloud, you can configure your browser to use a PAC file. A PAC file is a text file that directs a browser to forward traffic to a proxy server before going to the destination server. The Zscaler service hosts a default PAC file that uses geolocation technology to forward traffic to the nearest Public Service Edge for Internet & SaaS (ZIA). To learn more, see Using Default PAC Files to Forward Traffic to Internet & SaaS.
The following steps describe how to configure Google Chrome to use a PAC file on Windows systems:

blocks.item: Windows 7
The browser version used in this example is Google Chrome 53.0.2785.143 m. These steps might vary for different versions of Google Chrome.
To configure Google Chrome to use Zscaler’s PAC file URL:
From the navigating menu, go to Infrastructure > Internet & SaaS > Hosted PAC Files and copy the hosted URL to your clipboard.
See image.
Open Google Chrome, open the Chrome menu, then click Settings.
See image.
In the Settings window, click Show advanced settings.
See image.
Under Network, click Change proxy settings.
See image.
The Internet Properties window appears.
In the Internet Properties window, under the Connections tab, click LAN settings.
See image.
The Local Area Network (LAN) Settings window appears.
In the Local Area Network (LAN) Settings window, select Use automatic configuration script and paste the PAC file URL that you copied from the Zscaler Admin Console.
See image.
Click OK to save the configuration.
Windows 8 or later
The browser version used in this example is Google Chrome 96.0.4664.45. These steps might vary for different versions of Google Chrome.
To configure Google Chrome to use Zscaler’s PAC file URL:
From the navigating menu, go to Infrastructure > Internet & SaaS > Hosted PAC Files and copy the hosted URL to your clipboard.
See image.
Open Google Chrome, open the Chrome menu, then click Settings.
See image.
In the Settings window, click Advanced and then System.
Click Open your computer's proxy settings.
See image.
The Proxy settings page of your system appears.
On the Proxy settings page, enable Use setup script and then paste the PAC file URL that you copied from the Zscaler Admin Console into the Script address field.
See image.
Click Save to save the configuration.

blocks.text: For more information about getting started on the Zscaler service, see Getting Started.
